title: Syntax
summary: Write statements the JavaScript engine can parse.
refresher: JavaScript needs matching quotes, parentheses, brackets, and braces. Semicolons separate statements, braces group blocks, and `console.log(...)` displays a **value**.

blocks.body: JavaScript needs matching quotes, parentheses, brackets, and braces. Semicolons separate statements, braces group blocks, and `console.log(...)` displays a **value**. Write statements the JavaScript engine can parse.

JavaScript first parses the whole **file**. Parsing means checking whether the symbols form valid instructions. Only after that check can execution begin. This is why one missing quote can stop **output** from lines that appear earlier: the engine could not finish reading the program as a complete unit.

blocks.caption: The **string** closes correctly, and the template literal inserts the stored campus name.
A balanced statement gives the parser a clear ending.

blocks.body: Read the corrected line from the inside out: the quotes make a **string**, the parentheses pass it to `log`, and the semicolon ends the statement. If an error mentions an unexpected token, inspect the symbol just before the reported location too.

blocks.title: Watch this detail
blocks.body: An unexpected end of **input** often points to an earlier opening symbol that never received its matching closer.

blocks.why: The first choice balances its quotes and parentheses and uses the dot required before `log`.
The first line is a comment, so only the second statement executes.

output-01.title: Numbers add before they print
output-01.body: This checks whether the values are numbers or text. Number values use `+` for arithmetic before output happens.
output-01.notice: Evaluate the expression first, then decide what the output instruction shows.
output-01.mistake: Do not join digits like text unless quotes make them strings.

output-02.title: A variable name stands in for its value
output-02.body: The output line uses the stored value, not the variable name as literal text.
output-02.notice: Read the assignment first so the later output line has the value in place.
output-02.mistake: Do not choose an answer that prints the name itself when the code uses the variable.

output-03.title: Text plus text joins
output-03.body: When both sides are strings, `+` makes one longer string instead of doing arithmetic.
output-03.notice: Quotes are the clue that the values are text.
output-03.mistake: Do not add quoted digits as numbers unless the code converts them first.

output-04.title: Integer division keeps a whole result
output-04.body: This question tests the division rule for whole-number output in the selected language.
output-04.notice: Check whether the code asks for decimal division or a whole-number result.
output-04.mistake: Do not round up. Whole-number division keeps the complete groups.

output-05.title: Printing needs the exact output call
output-05.body: Type-in output questions care about the statement shape and the exact text being shown.
output-05.notice: Match the print/output function and include quotes around text.
output-05.mistake: Do not type only the word being printed when the question asks for a statement.

syntax-delimiter-01.title: Open delimiters need partners
syntax-delimiter-01.body: Brackets, parentheses, and quotes create a shape the parser must be able to close.
syntax-delimiter-01.notice: When code stops before running, scan for the opening symbol that never got closed.
syntax-delimiter-01.mistake: Do not debug the logic until the code can be parsed.

syntax-comment-01.title: Comments are skipped
syntax-comment-01.body: A comment can look like code, but the language ignores it when the program runs.
syntax-comment-01.notice: Only non-commented output statements affect what appears.
syntax-comment-01.mistake: Do not count a commented-out line as a printed line.

syntax-case-01.title: Names are case-sensitive
syntax-case-01.body: Capitalization can create a different name. Built-in words and user names must match exactly.
syntax-case-01.notice: If a familiar name fails, compare every letter including case.
syntax-case-01.mistake: Do not assume `Print` and `print` are the same spelling to the language.

syntax-line-break-01.title: Escapes can create invisible characters
syntax-line-break-01.body: Some characters inside strings describe formatting, such as moving output to the next line.
syntax-line-break-01.notice: Read escape sequences as one special character, not as ordinary letters.
syntax-line-break-01.mistake: Do not include the backslash text literally when the code asks for output.

syntax-block-01.title: Block headers need block syntax
syntax-block-01.body: A decision or loop header must clearly mark that a controlled body is coming next.
syntax-block-01.notice: Check the small symbol at the end of the header and the shape of the body below it.
syntax-block-01.mistake: Do not focus only on the condition and miss the punctuation that opens the block.
